sections.heading: EIP-8037/EIP-8038 Application Feedback
sections.summary: Rahul compiled spec feedback from affected teams; all high-severity issues on track to be fixed by mid-January.
sections.body:
- This feedback concerns the EIP-8037 spec design itself, not the security incidents found during outreach — all highs and most mediums are on track to adapt by mid-January.
- Uniswap complained about two execution branches depending on a user's transaction limit choice and that try-catch of calls is fundamentally broken.
- Zerodev and Enso raised a feature that was originally in EIP-8037 but dropped early; no public write-up exists explaining why it was removed.
- SnowBridge reported that AI coding assistants (Claude/Codex) refused to run the invariance-checking repo on their codebase, though this was not reproducible for other teams.
- Cowswap and Safe are not affected but are stressed by the invariant that gas-left can go up; they are actively triple-checking their code.
- [ChainSecurity published a write-up](https://gist.github.com/HubertRitzdorf-ChainSecurity/8689b3f0e7c0c33e3142c050928ad7a6) on preventing Glamsterdam-like problems in future, suggesting automated on-chain crawling at the EIP stage to detect affected contracts.
  - ChainSecurity notes that more communication helps but cannot fully solve the problem; specifying EVM invariants only protects new contracts, not already-deployed ones.
- Rahul recommended publishing a write-up of all design paths explored and rejected, since rationale currently lives scattered across Signal chats.
- Teams that were already prepared for Glamsterdam (e.g., Chainlink) reported they monitor [Forkcast](https://forkcast.org); most other teams learn about L1 changes via Twitter.
  - Rahul suggested pushing teams toward Forkcast and listing broken invariants per EIP there.
- Maria (EIP-8037 author) noted most questions are already answered in the EIP's rationale section and committed to updating it if anything is missing.
- Chat discussion highlighted that the EF's main social account is underutilized for surfacing protocol changes to application developers.

sections.heading: EIP-8037 Spec Change Decision Tree
sections.summary: Toni presented analysis of all explored spec changes; none fix invariants without introducing new issues, reinforcing the no-change default.
sections.body:
- Toni presented a decision tree covering ~7 potential spec change paths for the reservoir mechanism in EIP-8037, with pros and cons for each.
- Current spec (bottom-left of tree): gas-left can go up during transaction execution, breaking the monotonically-decreasing-gas invariant.
- Refunding the reservoir during execution (instead of into gas-left) does not fix any full invariant on its own; only when combined with no refund at all does it begin to fix the try-catch invariant (invariant 3: failed gas hands back state gas).
- The most radical option (right side of tree): no state refill during the transaction, refund only after execution. This would require many apps to specify much higher gas limits and massively complicate the spec.
  - ~300 historical transactions already showed problems under this variant; most fixable by raising gas limits, but the full impact is uncertain.
  - Forcing higher gas limits could increase griefing vectors against bundlers (e.g., ERC-4337) because the reservoir is opaque to gas-used accounting.
- Maria explained the reservoir exists because the 16 million transaction gas limit would otherwise cap state-heavy operations (e.g., contract deployment needing ~100 million gas), and removing it would defeat block-level access list parallelization.
- Andrew (Erigon) suggested trimming the reservoir and shipping less scaling now, adding it in Hegota if needed. Maria responded that without the reservoir, the transaction limit would have to be raised so much that attack blocks could defeat all parallelization.
- Łukasz (Nethermind) noted he found no transactions that couldn't be fixed by raising the gas limit (sometimes beyond 16M, but within the reservoir allowance), and acknowledged the spec-change option is appealing but not fully vetted.
- Luis Pinto expressed concern about breaking EVM invariants, suggesting it might be preferable to have users post more gas than to break fundamental execution semantics.
- Toni's conclusion: no silver bullet exists; any change would require re-analysis of all already-contacted apps, so the default path remains no spec change.
- Decision deferred to ACDC on Thursday, where the spec-change question and Hoodi testnet scheduling will be locked in together.
  - Ansgar noted in chat that any change now would cost ~2 months delay (give up testnets this year, reassess, re-test, testnet rollouts Feb–March, mainnet April) with the risk of ending up shipping the current version anyway.

sections.heading: ChainSecurity Opinion on Fork Development Process
sections.summary: ChainSecurity's post on improving future fork processes was shared for async reading; Hubert was not on the call.
sections.body:
- Mario shared [ChainSecurity's opinion post](https://gist.github.com/HubertRitzdorf-ChainSecurity/8689b3f0e7c0c33e3142c050928ad7a6) authored by Hubert Ritzdorf on how to prevent Glamsterdam-like issues in future forks.
- Hubert was not present on the call; the post was shared for client devs to read asynchronously.
- Dustin questioned in chat why analysis was done in private repos given nothing was deployed beyond Sepolia; Francesco noted a reason was that the fork might have shipped with some contracts affected but not fixed.

sections.heading: Hegota Devnet Status
sections.summary: Bogota devnet-2 is finalizing with 5 ELs; a new Daisugi devnet-0 with frames and leanSPHINCS transactions is live; Heze devnet-3 was torn down.
sections.body:
- Bogota devnet-2: 5 EL clients present; Erigon is the only one missing. Network is finalizing.
- [Daisugi devnet-0](https://dora.daisugi-devnet-0.ethpandaops.io/) launched by PK with frames and STARK aggregation, running Nethermind + Lighthouse with 4000 validators.
  - Finalizing and processing leanSPHINCS transactions.
  - [EthPandaOps notes on Daisugi devnet-0](https://notes.ethereum.org/@ethpandaops/daisugi-devnet-0)
- Heze devnet-3 was torn down because quick slots were removed from scope.

sections.heading: Bogota Devnet-3 Scoping
sections.summary: No consensus to scope Bogota devnet-3 this week; only Nethermind and Erigon favored it; decision deferred to next week pending frames spec progress.
sections.body:
- Mario asked EL client teams whether Bogota devnet-3 should happen and what EIPs it should include. Combined Hegota devnet-0 was already ruled out at ACDE last Thursday due to unresolved FOCIL status.
- **ethrex**: No to devnet-3 scope expansion; keep current Bogota scope as baseline; prioritize frame hardening, mempool testing, and EIP-8151 application compatibility. Proposed a minimal leanSPHINCS EIP ([EIP PR #12672](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12672)) for forward-compatible PQ support in Hegota.
- **Nethermind (Łukasz)**: Yes to devnet-3; proposed adding EIP-8279 (Block Access List Byte Floor), EIP-8131 (Unified Transaction Content Floor), and potentially EIP-7907 (Meter Contract Code Size, still PFI) for scaling.
- **Geth (lightclient)**: No to devnet-3 until frames spec is finalized for forward compatibility with EIP-8288; spec questions are still a few weeks from resolution. No benefit to launching a devnet without a credible spec.
- **Besu (Justin Florentine)**: Concurred with Geth; initially considered EIP-8077 but withdrew it pending clarity on mempool rule simplification. Asked whether VOPS-like mempool protections would be dialed back.
- **Erigon (Andrew)**: Yes to a minimal devnet-3; proposed EIP-5920 (PAY opcode) and EIP-7668 (Remove Bloom Filters) as cleanups, plus PQ direction work. Cautioned against expanding scope too much.
- **Reth (Dragan)**: No strong opinion; defers to other clients.
- **Nimbus EL (Dustin)**: No strong opinion; PQ is the priority.
- **Specs team (Jochem)**: No new EIPs unrelated to PQ work. Flagged that EIP-4758 (Deactivate SELFDESTRUCT) is on Bogota devnet-2 but EIP-8360 (TCREATE) is not on any devnet — either remove 4758 or add 8360 to give smart contract devs an alternative.
  - Andrew and Ivan agreed; Andrew strongly favors finally removing SELFDESTRUCT. Ivan leaned toward removing EIP-4758 from scope rather than adding EIP-8360.
- **Guru (specs)**: Noted EIP-8298 (SETCODEFROM) is on devnet-2 and solutions for EOA-to-smart-account migration on frames depend on its SFI status; asked clients to review it.
- **EthPandaOps (Stefan)**: Proposed a [minimal devnet-3 scope](https://notes.ethereum.org/@ethpandaops/bogota-devnet-3) with only Remove Bloom Filters and Remove Storage Clear Refund/Refund Cap as new EIPs, acknowledging the call's vibe pointed away from a near-term devnet-3.
- Final tally: Nethermind and Erigon in favor; Geth and ethrex against; Besu, Reth, Nimbus EL unsure.
- Decision deferred to next week's ACDT, pending progress on frames spec.
- Marius noted in chat: "I think doing a devnet for the purpose of a devnet isn't good. We should be deliberate about why we want a new devnet."

sections.heading: Frames Forward Compatibility with EIP-8288
sections.summary: Core question is whether PQ proof support belongs in a proof/dependency frame or the signature list; no decision; discussion continues async in pq-el.
sections.body:
- lightclient identified the central open question: should post-quantum proof support (leanSPHINCS, leanPCS) be added to frames via a proof/dependency frame or via the signature list?
- Original EIP-8288 vision: user-defined code (e.g., RISC-V) would be deployed on-chain at a target address; the protocol would construct the STARK proof over that code's execution, requiring no proving from the user.
- With leanPCS, the model shifts: users must construct the proof locally into a format the protocol can verify. This means the protocol supports a small allow-list (leanSPHINCS + leanPCS), making it similar to what the signature list already does.
- Toni noted that even in EIP-8288's current spec, the proof frame requires the target address to be empty, suggesting no on-chain code execution was intended; leanPCS EIP uses an arbitrary scheme identifier.
- Toni's view: both approaches work; since dependencies are closer to signatures than to frames, the signature list is simpler.
- lightclient reported pushback from L2s who find signature list harder to extend than adding a precompile, which currently makes him lean toward the proof frame approach.
- Key edge case: when users don't use leanSPHINCS or leanPCS and use arbitrary cryptographic schemes.
  - With a proof frame, non-whitelisted targets would not be aggregated; call data would remain intact.
  - Signature data commitment is needed to prevent malicious parties from stripping proof data in transit (e.g., L2 update proofs). Frames currently handle this via committing to data length in the arbitrary scheme type.
- Kevaundray outlined the relationship: leanSPHINCS = F is SPHINCS signing (proof = signature); leanSTARK = F is a RISC-V/Wasm VM (proof = STARK); leanPCS = minimal building block exposing just the polynomial commitment scheme.
- Ivan clarified that leanSPHINCS and leanPCS will coexist — regular users use leanSPHINCS signatures; leanPCS serves privacy protocols and computation proofs. leanPCS is not required for PQ but enables subsidized proofs.
  - Ivan proposed a phased devnet plan: pq-el-devnet-0 (frames + leanSPHINCS claims, no aggregation), pq-el-devnet-1 (+ builder aggregation with recursive verifier), pq-el-devnet-2 (+ mempool aggregation).
- Dragan (Reth) noted the opportunity to have any signature accessible to contracts without routing through call data, and emphasized parallel signature recovery as important for performance.
- Agreement: continue discussion async in pq-el and 8141 Discord channels; revisit on next ACDT or ACDE.
- Ivan encouraged all EL teams to review EIP-8288 and the dependency frame proposal, and asked in chat who could gather all the sources for the discussion.
